title: Hyphenate Raises $45M at $270M Valuation to Automate Enterprise Finance
summary:
The startup founded by alumni of IIT Madras has secured latest-stage funding to automate the reconciliation of disparate corporate finance systems. The $45M Series A investment, which values Hyphenate at $270M, will support the development of a platform that analyzes a company's spreadsheets, system logs, and emails to perform work across ERP, payroll, and billing functions.

Launched in 2024 by former Microsoft engineers Ram and Ajay, the company has already acquired several Fortune 500 customers. The founders, who were recruited by Microsoft from India in 2016, designed the software to target chief financial and accounting officers by providing persistent AI agents capable of handling company-specific judgment and high-accuracy financial reporting.

selectedTweets.text:
@HyphenateAI  has raised a $45M Series A!
When @JayaGup10  and I first met Ram and Ajay, our “quick meeting” quickly turned into a 6-hour dinner. 

Ram and Ajay first crossed paths at IIT Madras, a year apart.

Ram graduated top of his class and sold his first startup before finishing college. Ajay was an ACM-ICPC world finalist - think the Olympics of coding. 

Each year, a Microsoft VP flew to India’s top IIT colleges and hand picked 2 graduates to bring back to the US. In 2016, it was these two. 

After nearly a decade at Microsoft, Ram partnering with enterprises like Walmart and Coca-Cola and Ajay rebuilding the company’s internal billing platform, they found the problem that would become Hyphenate.

Finance stacks are full of systems that don’t talk to each other: ERP, payroll, billing, CRM. Finance teams spend their days stitching together and reconciling in Excel.

Before Hyphenate, companies had two half-fixes. They could buy a patchwork of point solutions or hire a vendor whose engineers build agents for you.

Ram and Ajay saw a third option: one platform that learns how a company’s finance team works, from its own spreadsheets, emails and system logs, and then does the work across the whole function.

Finance has some of the most risk-averse buyers in enterprise software. Every number has to be 100% accurate. That’s exactly the kind of hard engineering problem these two love.

So in 2024, they left Microsoft and started Hyphenate.

At that dinner, Jaya and I were drawn in by their clarity of thought, technical depth, and firsthand understanding of the problem.  Ram is the son of a CFO of public-company in India, and Ajay helped rebuild how Microsoft bills its cloud customers.

We led their seed round. With founders like Ram and Ajay, it was impossible not to. 

Proud to be back for their Series A.
Congratulations to @ramkris, @ajkrish95, and the entire Hyphenate team.
